title: Advantages and Disadvantages of Piezoelectric Composites
content: For nearly a century, piezoelectric materials have been extensively studied for their diverse applications, including sensors, actuators, energy harvesting systems, and biomedical devices. This paper explores the piezoelectric effect, along with the advantages and limitations of various material groups with a particular focus on the composite materials; and suggests potential solutions to address some of their challenges. This was done through combining information from a number of papers providing an overview of piezoelectric research. This study showed that while composites offer significant advantages in terms of performance, they also present certain challenges like low Curie temperatures, the  difficulty to fabricate at nanoscale levels, and poor resistance to high temperatures and moisture; with the major challenge being the difficulty to balance flexibility and piezoelectricity in polymer composites. It was found that by incorporating the 3-3-3 connectivity design, both flexibility and high piezoelectric performance could be achieved. This means that this connectivity design is a viable solution for composites, without compromising between flexibility and a high piezoelectric constant. Future directions of research could focus on advancing material development, improving fabrication techniques, and integrating emerging technologies.
